ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17, with Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, administered by FINTRAC. Corporate UBO governance: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c. B-9, which requires a register of individuals with significant control (ISC); if federal incorporation is elected, Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44, as amended by the 2024 corporate transparency framework, applies. Securities-specific AML/CFT and registration governance: Securities Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. S-4, National Instrument 31-103, and applicable CIRO/IIROC dealer rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of valid passport of each director and each individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or equivalent official of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if source jurisdiction is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of corporate existence for any corporate shareholder, parent entity, or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction company registry or competent registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency, register of directors, and register of officers of the parent entity or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or sealing authority of the relevant corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth statement and certified bank or brokerage reference letter for each significant individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Executing individual and issuing financial institution in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English translation of any non-English corporate, UBO, or evidentiary document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Accredited certified translator in the country of origin or in Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator's certificate notarized and, where the translation forms part of a notarial exhibit, authenticated by Apostille or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, Canadian sanctions lists under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act, and the Criminal Code (Canada) terrorist listing. Politically exposed persons (PEP) screening must follow FINTRAC definitions and thresholds, including foreign PEPs, former PEPs, and domestic PEPs at prescribed high-risk positions. Enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, ongoing transaction monitoring, and independent AML/CFT risk assessment are mandatory for a high-risk securities brokerage registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Registry Search and Online Services) for Alberta incorporation; Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre for federal incorporation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names under Alberta law must be in English and/or French script using Roman alphabetic characters, Arabic numerals, and allowed punctuation. Names must be distinguishable within Alberta. Non-Latin script names require a transliteration into Roman characters and must be searchable in English or French. A NUANS search report is required for both provincial and federal incorporation. Names suggesting or designating restricted regulated activities require evidence of the appropriate securities, banking, trust, or insurance license.

stage_1.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant shall file a written request for reconsideration with the Alberta Corporate Registry Director within 30 days of the refusal, attaching the original NUANS name search report, a statement of distinguishability, and any regulatory license evidence needed to support a sensitive token. If the administrative reconsideration is denied, the applicant may apply for judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Rules of Court and the applicable provisions of the Business Corporations Act. For federal incorporation under the CBCA, the equivalent appeal is a written objection to the Director of Corporations Canada within the applicable statutory window, followed by judicial review in the Federal Court or the provincial superior court, as applicable.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 12-14 (incorporation), s. 20 (certificate of incorporation), s. 101 (registered office), s. 111 (directors); Electronic Transactions Act (Alberta) recognizing electronic signatures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, operated through authorized Registry Agents and the Alberta Corporate Access online portal; paper filings accepted at the Corporate Registry counters in Edmonton and Calgary.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 Articles of Incorporation, accompanied by Form 2 Notice of Registered Office and Form 3 Notice of Directors; the Certificate of Incorporation is issued as conclusive evidence of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; no statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit is required. Shares may be issued at nominal par value (CAD 0.01 per share). Regulatory net capital and client trust-account segregation requirements apply separately at the securities dealer licensing stage under National Instrument 31-103 and CIRO rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the incorporation under Alberta law is ratified; (2) the subscription for 1,000 Class A Common Shares at $0.01 per share is accepted; (3) the registered office is fixed at Suite 2200, 350 7th Avenue SW, Calgary, AB T2P 3N9; (4) the CEO, CFO and Corporate Secretary are appointed; (5) those officers may open segregated client trust and operating accounts at a Schedule I Canadian bank, file the CIRO dealer membership application and Alberta Securities Commission registration, and pay all filing fees; and (6) the Corporate Secretary is directed to maintain all statutory registers and minutes at the registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized Alberta Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request an official NUANS name search through an authorized registry agent; verify the proposed corporate name is distinct from existing Alberta and federal corporate names; obtain the NUANS report with a search number and reserve the name for filings.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request and payment receipt
List of three proposed corporate names in order of preference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a conflict is returned, select the next preferred name and rerun the NUANS search; a written reconsideration may be submitted to the Corporate Registry within 30 days of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Formation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and corporate counsel / authorized Alberta Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 1 Articles of Incorporation, Form 2 Notice of Registered Office and Form 3 Notice of Directors; set the authorized capital structure with 1,000 Class A common voting shares at par value CAD 0.01; specify the Calgary registered office and the first director; execute by incorporator using electronic signature under the Electronic Transactions Act (Alberta).
required_dossiers: Form 1 Articles of Incorporation completed and executed
Form 2 Notice of Registered Office completed and executed
Form 3 Notice of Directors completed and executed
Director consent forms fully signed
Government-issued photo identification for each incorporator and director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises a completeness deficiency, amend the affected Form and resubmit; no notarial attestation is required for standard Alberta share-capital incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to the Alberta Corporate Registry and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via Alberta Corporate Access online portal or approved Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed formation documents electronically through the Alberta Corporate Access portal or lodge physically with a Corporate Registry counter; pay the applicable CAD 350 incorporation fee; retain the Corporate Access file acknowledgement and payment receipt.
required_dossiers: Executed Form 1 Articles of Incorporation
Executed Form 2 Notice of Registered Office
Executed Form 3 Notice of Directors
NUANS name search report
Director consents
Government-issued identification for officers and directors
Payment confirmation for incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, respond to the Registry correction notice within 30 days by filing corrected documents; corrected filings are generally accepted without an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Index Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Monitor the Corporate Access account for the electronic Certificate of Incorporation; verify the corporate name, number, registered office and director information; download the certificate and open the corporate minute book and statutory register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Alberta Corporate Registry
Corporate Access file acknowledgement
Internal corporate minute book and share register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical or clerical errors, apply to the Corporate Registry for a certificate of correction under the ABCA; an amended certificate will be issued upon proof of the error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, First Board Resolution and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution of the Board adopting the pro-forma first board resolution; approve the issue of 1,000 Class A common shares to the subscribers; adopt the bylaws; appoint the CEO, CFO and Corporate Secretary; execute share certificates and record all transfers in the securities register.
required_dossiers: First board resolution signed by all directors
Company bylaws
Share subscription agreements
Share certificates for Class A common shares
Securities register and directors' register
Minute book opened at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect is discovered in the share allotment, the Board may pass a corrective resolution and reissue the affected share certificates; the corporate secretary must minute the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Registration and Business Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation, apply for the federal Business Number through CRA Business Registration Online; register the corporate income tax account, GST/HST account (where relevant), and any payroll account if employees will be engaged; confirm the fiscal year-end and the registered office address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation from the Alberta Corporate Registry
Registered office address confirmation
Director and officer government-issued identification
Completed CRA Business Registration Information form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA issues a mismatch or clarification letter, correct the registration data through My Business Account or direct the corporation to the CRA business enquiries line within the stated response period to avoid account suspension.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Initial Return and Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual/information return with the Alberta Corporate Registry to confirm the registered office and director details; complete any required updates to the corporate register and ensure the corporate records are kept at the registered office in Calgary.
required_dossiers: Corporate annual return / information return form
Notice of directors and registered office (updated if changed)
Certificate of Incorporation reference number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is assessed with a penalty, file the return and pay any late fee; an administrative refund or penalty relief may be requested under the Registry's voluntary disclosure policy.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Securities Commission (ASC) Registration Division and the Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO), formerly IIROC and MFDA; additional oversight by the Alberta Financial Services and Consumer Affairs regulatory stream under the Securities Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c S-4.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as an Investment Dealer under National Instrument 31-103 Registration Requirements, Exemptions and Ongoing Registrant Obligations and Dealer Membership with CIRO; together with membership in the Canadian Investor Protection Fund (CIPF) for retail client business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas, and applicable municipal licensing authority (City of Calgary Planning and Development)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Class 5 financial services; no industrial processing, stationary combustion source, substantial wastewater discharge or hazardous waste generation attributable to the brokerage operations. No full EIA report is required for an office-based enterprise.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for regulated process discharges; the office fit-out and leased premises must meet the Alberta Fire Code, Calgary Building Code wastewater/ventilation standards, and the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act waste management rules for e-waste and confidential paper disposal. Electronic media destruction must align with the Personal Information Protection Act (Alberta).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Calgary Fire Department and Alberta Fire Code compliance for the registered office; structural load clearance and building occupancy permit from the City of Calgary; workplace safety clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code, including emergency evacuation planning, first aid, ergonomic and security requirements for a retail brokerage operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Incorporate under either the Canada Business Corporations Act (federal) or the Alberta Business Corporations Act (provincial). Upon incorporation, register with the CRA using Form RC1 or through the Business Registration Online (BRO) service. The Canadian Business Number (BN) is the statutory tax identifier, with program accounts for corporate income tax (RP), GST/HST (RT), and, if applicable, payroll (RP) and import/export (RM) accounts. Non-resident corporations with Canadian-source income must additionally file an income tax return under section 150 of the Income Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — Canadian-resident corporations are separate taxable entities subject to Canadian income tax under Part I of the Income Tax Act; there is no pass-through election for a Business Corporation. The corporation is subject to federal and Alberta income tax, and is taxed on worldwide income if resident in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general check-the-box election. Entity classification is determined by the incorporation statute. Available elections include: the functional currency election (Income Tax Act s.261); the preferred-election to treat a dividend as a capital dividend (s.83(2)); and, for hybrid mismatch, the election under subsection 18.4(8) to exclude certain hybrid instrument amounts from the limitation rules. These elections do not alter the corporation's per se taxable status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) — federally administered VAT; in Alberta, only the 5% federal GST applies as there is no provincial general sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — a person (including a non-resident) making taxable supplies in Canada must register for GST/HST if their worldwide taxable supplies exceed this small-supplier threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time clearance or digital stamping regime exists in Canada. E-invoices are permitted if they satisfy the information requirements under subsections 223(1) and 224(1) of the Excise Tax Act. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically in certain cases; however, there is no API-based pre-authorization mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The supply of financial services (including offshore securities brokerage) to a non-resident may be zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part VI, subsection 6 of the Excise Tax Act, provided the service is not for use, enjoyment, or benefit in Canada and is not supplied to an individual in Canada at the time of performance. For goods exports, zero-rating applies when goods are exported by the supplier or on their behalf and documentary evidence of export is retained. Canada does not impose a statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is a common due-diligence convention for maintaining proof-of-export documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration (CBSA) or CBSA A8/A6 account export report
Bill of lading or airway waybill
Proof of export / delivery confirmation (e.g., signed proof of delivery, customs release documents)
Service contract and confirmatory non-resident status certificate (for zero-rated financial services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where zero-rating is claimed incorrectly, the CRA can reassess within four years (or longer in cases of misrepresentation, neglect, or wilful default), claw back denied input tax credits, and apply penalties. The penalty for making a false statement in a return, knowingly or under gross negligence, is the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the tax that would have been payable may be assessed under s.285.1, plus applicable interest. Criminal tax evasion charges may be pursued under s.381 of the Excise Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII member with fully convertible current and capital accounts. The Canadian dollar floats freely, and no exchange-control permits, quantitative limits, or conversion authorization requirements are imposed on resident or non-resident parties. Profit remittances and dividends are subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax and applicable tax treaty rate reductions, but there is no exchange-control clearance or foreign investment repatriation approval requirement. All cross-border wires remain subject to sanctions screening and to FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose a statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in CAD or convertible foreign currency at the exporter's discretion, subject only to applicable record-keeping, financial-crime compliance, and tax reporting requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD) and segregated client trust account via RBC Investor & Treasury Services
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (CAD/USD)
International Operational Account with trade settlement and FX forward lines
Operational Account (CAD/USD) and CDS depository settlement account
Operational Account and integrated custody/settlement package for broker-dealers

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium for ancillary operating treasury and unacceptable for client money segregation. Canadian law requires segregated client monies to be held with a licensed Canadian depository institution and/or a CIRO-approved custodian. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut) may operate in Canada only as money service businesses, not as banks; they can support low-value multi-currency float accounts after FINTRAC MSB registration, but all client-money, margin, and regulatory settlement accounts must be held with a Tier-1 Canadian bank or an approved trust company.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a high-risk, non-resident-owned securities brokerage, Tier-1 Canadian banks will normally require at least one authorized director or senior signatory to complete an in-person KYC interview at a branch or before a bank-approved notary/video-confirm agent. Remote onboarding can be offered to passive ultimate beneficial owners with certified electronic identity verification, but full account activation typically requires physical presence of the Compliance Officer / Anti-Money Laundering Officer, board resolutions, certified constitutional documents, and source-of-funds evidence. A certificate from Canadian legal counsel is customarily required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque offshore ownership chain or UBO residing in a high-risk / tax-haven jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized shareholder register; full chain-of-title to individual UBOs; passport and residential address verification for every UBO; source-of-wealth statement; audited group financials; tax residency certificates; local counsel legal opinion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mailbox-company profile or insufficient business substance in Alberta.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed office lease in Calgary or Edmonton; current utility invoice; payroll records for local licensed officers; board resolution designating Alberta as the principal place of business; premises photographs/video; service contract with a local compliance and AML provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction flows from or to unregulated third-party processors, crypto exchanges, or high-risk payment corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete counterparty due-diligence file; licensing status and AML policy for each processor; business rationale memorandum; contract and product documentation; historical transaction volume/value analytics; FINTRAC MSB registration evidence where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Retail CFDs/derivatives flagged as high-risk by the bank's legal, compliance, or reputational risk committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provincial securities licence (Alberta Securities Commission / AFSA exemption); CIRO dealer membership or written compliance regime; AML compliance program; investor appropriateness and leverage policies; risk disclosure materials; capital adequacy computations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or rapid inbound equity injection (e.g., CAD 1M+) from a related non-resident parent without clear documentary trace.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorizing the capital call; share subscription agreement; paid-in capital ledger; source-of-funds records (bank statements, audited financial statements, parent tax filings); updated constating documents; legal confirmation that funds are not criminally derived.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital as SWIFT MT103 customer credits (or MT202 bank-to-bank credits) to the Alberta operational account in CAD or USD. Include a clear remittance narrative such as 'Capital contribution - [Legal Name]', 'Shareholder loan disbursement', or 'Equity subscription proceeds', together with the corporate account/reference number. The receiving bank will verify the payment against the board resolution and capital ledger, apply sanctions screening, and report under FINTRAC electronic funds transfer rules for transactions above CAD 10,000. For capital injections above CAD 1M, provide a director's resolution, executed subscription agreement, UBO source-of-funds file, and external legal confirmation before crediting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for customer payouts and counterparty margin transfers; MT202/MT202 COV for interbank USD settlement; and MT700 documentary letters of credit for trade-finance disbursements. For CAD clearing, use the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS/Lynx RTGS); for USD, use Fedwire or CHIPS through the Canadian bank's correspondent; for eligible FX-spot pairs, use CLS Bank's payment-versus-payment mechanism. Canadian-listed equity trades clear through CDS/CDSX with delivery-versus-payment settlement against the broker's omnibus or segregated client accounts. Commingling of house and client funds is prohibited; all client disbursements must originate from the segregated client trust account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards between CAD and USD and other G10 crosses
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted or emerging-market currencies such as CNY, KRW, and INR
Cross-currency swaps for long-dated funding and asset-liability hedging
Vanilla FX options, including plain put/call structures, excluding binary, barrier, or exotic options
Listed FX futures and options traded on CME or Cboe

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of the corporation's anniversary date or the previous annual return filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative dissolution after 30 days of default notice; late filing penalty of $100; reinstatement fee of $100 plus penalties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the corporation is a reporting issuer, has more than 50 shareholders, or if required by articles of incorporation or shareholder resolution
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Canada

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of directors and shareholdings as part of the Annual Return filing; beneficial ownership information updated upon transfers and confirmed annually under FINTRAC AML guidelines for high-risk entities

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general corporate rate (federal Part I 15% + Alberta provincial 8%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction: 11% combined (federal 9% + Alberta 2%) on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income; the deduction remains available to an active securities brokerage, while a corporation whose principal purpose is earning income from property (specified investment business) must employ more than 5 full-time employees to qualify. No general tax holidays apply to Alberta securities brokerages. Part IV refundable tax of 38 1/3% applies to portfolio dividends received by a private corporation and is refunded on taxable dividend distributions. Federal non-capital losses may be carried forward 20 years and back 3 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (consolidated federal and Alberta return; Alberta tax is computed on T2 Schedule 5 and administered by the CRA under the Alberta Tax Collection Agreement). Electronic filing via CRA E-filing through approved T2 software or the CRA 'Represent a Client' / 'My Business Account' portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; final income tax balance due within 2 months after fiscal year-end (3 months for CCPCs).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, 9-digit Business Number (BN) with RC0001 program code, fiscal year-end date, province of residence and permanent establishment code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Alberta through a permanent establishment must obtain a CRA BN and file a T2 even if no tax is payable; include the Alberta PE address and the treaty article under which the PE is recognized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue: gross commissions, mark-ups, spreads, and fee income from retail equities, CFD and derivative execution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue attributable to the Canadian PE; foreign-source brokerage income must be separately reconciled on the T2 foreign-income schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductions: clearing and execution fees, regulatory levies (ASC/CIRO), hedging and CFD swap costs, software licensing, payroll, and office rent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses reasonably allocated to the Canadian PE; head-office allocations must satisfy the arm's length standard under ITA s. 247 and be supported by contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: reconciliation of accounting income to tax income, including application of non-capital losses, foreign tax credits, and GAAR adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxable income on the Canadian-source basis; attach a treaty position statement if no PE is asserted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I tax after deductions and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled corporations are not CCPCs and are ineligible for the small business deduction; apply the 15% general federal rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta corporate income tax at 8% general rate (or 2% small business rate for CCPCs), including Alberta tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Alberta statutory allocation formula using the PE's gross revenue and payroll in Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward reconciliation; foreign affiliate disclosures; Part XIII withholding returns for dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach T106 (non-arm's length transactions), T1134 (foreign affiliates) and NR4 summaries; remit Part XIII WHT within 15 days after the end of the month in which the payment was made.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month of delay, capped at 12 months; a second-filing false or negligent return attracts 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months; interest at the CRA prescribed rate compounds daily. Failure to file information returns (T106/NR4/T1134) carries additional separate daily penalties.
